title: Whole-person health
summary: Explains UnitedHealthcare's whole-person health approach for employers, covering medical, pharmacy, behavioral health, specialty, financial wellness and wellness programs.

atoms.title: What whole-person health means
atoms.question: What is a whole-person approach to employee health benefits?
atoms.text: Focusing only on the medical side of an employee's health does not offer a complete picture. A whole-person approach addresses an individual's physical, mental, financial and overall health and well-being needs. UnitedHealthcare says it has the breadth of products and solutions to help ensure an employer's benefits strategy addresses all the factors that may influence employee health and well-being.
questions: Why do employers take a whole-person approach to benefits?

atoms.title: Employees see well-being as connected
atoms.question: Do employees see physical and mental well-being as connected?
atoms.text: According to the survey cited in UnitedHealthcare's whole-person health video, 95% of surveyed employees said physical, mental, emotional and social well-being are all connected. By addressing pharmacy, financial and behavioral health needs and more, UnitedHealthcare says employers can take a holistic approach that may lead to a healthier, more productive workforce and significant cost savings.
questions: What share of employees say mental and physical health are connected?

atoms.title: Medical and pharmacy rank as top benefits
atoms.question: Which benefits do employers rank as most important?
atoms.text: Surveyed employers rank medical benefits as the No. 1 most important benefit to offer employees and pharmacy benefits as No. 2, according to UnitedHealthcare Whole-Person Health Research conducted between February 20, 2024 and April 25, 2024. UnitedHealthcare says it offers a variety of medical plans and targeted clinical programs that treat the whole person, not just the condition at hand.
questions: What do employers consider the most important benefit?
How important is pharmacy coverage to employers?

atoms.title: Integrated medical and pharmacy benefits
atoms.question: Why manage medical and pharmacy benefits together?
atoms.text: Around 55% of an employer's total drug spend applies to specialty medications, and many drugs are covered under both benefits. In an integrated model, UnitedHealthcare reviews medical and pharmacy claims to better advocate for employees on when to use their medical benefit and when to use their pharmacy benefit. When managed together, care can be more coordinated, with better outcomes, lower costs and simpler experiences.

atoms.title: Mental health conditions affect employees and productivity
atoms.question: How common are mental health disorders among working-age adults?
atoms.text: Approximately 15% of working-age adults currently live with a mental health disorder, and depression and anxiety alone drain $1T from the global economy annually through lost productivity, according to the World Health Organization. UnitedHealthcare says behavioral health benefits can help ensure employees and their families have access to mental health support, with a guided experience to find needed care.

atoms.title: Dental, vision and hearing are essential benefits
atoms.question: Are dental, vision and hearing benefits essential?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare says dental, vision and hearing benefits are not extras but essential benefits, because a person's mouth, eyes and ears often serve as indicators of overall health and well-being. It says specialty benefits may help detect early signs of serious conditions and reduce long-term costs.
questions: Why should employers offer dental, vision and hearing coverage?

atoms.title: Financial stress and employee well-being
atoms.question: How does financial stress affect employees at work?
atoms.text: Personal financial concerns can affect employees' mental health, productivity and focus at work. U.S. employees spend more than 8 hours a week managing personal finances, and half of that occurs during work hours, according to Harvard Business Review. UnitedHealthcare offers integrated solutions such as flexible spending accounts and financial protection benefits to help employees manage financial health.

atoms.title: Wellness programs and fewer sick days
atoms.question: Do wellness programs reduce sick days?
atoms.text: Making healthier lifestyle choices may help reduce the likelihood of developing a chronic illness while also improving quality of life. UnitedHealthcare cites a Wellhub study stating that 89% said employees take fewer sick days as a result of their well-being program. UnitedHealthcare says it has wellness programs designed to foster healthier, more productive workforces.
